key_insight: OmniFabric improves single-image 3D garment reconstruction by synthesizing coherent UV-space textures, helping garments look consistent across the whole surface instead of having baked-in lighting artifacts. This makes reconstructed clothing more usable for realistic rendering, relighting, and downstream simulation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of generating production-ready 3D garment textures from a single image. Existing methods often produce inconsistent UV textures or accidentally encode shadows and illumination into the texture map, reducing realism and physical usability.
method: Generates garment textures directly in UV space to preserve global surface consistency across the 3D asset.
Focuses on separating appearance from scene illumination so the texture remains clean and relightable.
Targets reconstruction quality suitable for production pipelines rather than just visually plausible previews.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work advances practical 3D asset creation by improving the texture quality bottleneck in single-image garment reconstruction. It is especially relevant for digital fashion, virtual try-on, game asset creation, and physically based simulation workflows.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of standard texture baking vs coherent UV-space synthesis

paper_title: OmniFabric: Coherent UV Space Texture Synthesis for 3D Garment Reconstruction
paper_authors: Ding-Jiun Huang, Yuanhao Wang, Cheng Zhang, Hugo Bertiche, Alexandru-Eugen Ichim
